151015.creator: Unknown maker

editorial.note: This extraordinary album has 50 paintings on a variety of religious subjects. They were likely created by several master craftsmen to share with studio apprentices as models for fulfilling commissions.

You can identify the leading figures, even without knowing the story: the seated old man is Jacob, and the boy standing next to him Benjamin, the youngest of his eleven sons. They are rendered in detail.

155399.title: The Entombment, over a Sketch of an Executioner
155399.creator: Rembrandt van Rijn

editorial.note: This expressive drawing shows how Rembrandt translated his observations of human suffering into the biblical stories he depicted. Christ is truly dead: his body is stiff, and his hair hangs down.

Daniel was awarded a high court position by the Babylonian king Darius. His envious enemies devised a ruse to have Daniel thrown to the lions; however, the wild creatures left the praying Daniel unharmed.

Christ squats among his apostles and washes Peter’s feet above a water basin. Peter objected to Christ humbling himself in this way. He could not understand that Christ, with this servile task, expressed his superior humanity.

155415.title: David Hearing the News of Uriah’s Death
155415.creator: Rembrandt van Rijn

editorial.note: In deze psychologisch zeer complexe tekening spreekt de lichaamstaal van koning David boekdelen.

155417.title: The Angel Appearing to Joseph in his Dream
155417.creator: Rembrandt van Rijn

editorial.note: Shortly after Jesus’s birth, an angel appeared to Joseph in a dream, urging him to flee into Egypt with the Virgin and Child. Fearing the ‘King of the Jews’, the local ruler King Herod ordered all newly born boys to be killed.

155419.title: Tobias and the Angel Taking Leave of Raguel
155419.creator: Rembrandt van Rijn

editorial.note: The sadness of leave-taking is central in this scene. Accompanied by his bride, Sarah, Tobias is about to leave his homeland to cure his blind father, Tobit. He is embraced by his beloved fatherin-law, Raguel.

Christ healed a leper by simply touching him. Rembrandt initially showed Christ taking hold of the afflicted man’s hand. He changed his mind and covered both hands with opaque lead white, which has oxidized over time.

After suffering a crushing defeat against the Israelites, the Canaanite army general Sisera imagined he was safe in the tent of the Jewish Jael. However, as soon as he fell asleep, she killed him, driving a tent peg through his head.
